patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — HubSpot documents a broader use-case set; Mailchimp is narrower/specialist.

HubSpot documents a broader use-case set; Mailchimp is narrower/specialist. Choose HubSpot only if your buying job matches “AI-powered customer platform with free forever CRM, plus paid Smart CRM seats and Sales/Ma” rather than Mailchimp's shape. Choose Mailchimp only if your buying job matches “Email marketing with CRM features; freemium entry (secondary category: marketing).” rather than HubSpot's shape. Workflow advantage: HubSpot leans pipeline-management, sales-automation; Mailchimp leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — HubSpot documents a broader use-case set; Mailchimp is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: HubSpot is AI-powered customer platform with free forever CRM, plus paid Smart CRM seats and Sales/Marketing/Service hubs for growing teams.; Mailchimp is Email marketing with CRM features; freemium entry (secondary category: marketing)..
- Company-size focus: HubSpot (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Mailchimp (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: HubSpot-leaning pipeline-management, sales-automation, account-management vs Mailchimp-leaning —.
- Researched limits: HubSpot — Smart CRM / Customer Platform seats and Sales Hub seats are separate ladders with different list prices; buying 'HubSpot' often means mixing Free CRM, Smart CRM seats, and hub seats.; Mailchimp — Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform.

Limitations — HubSpot: Smart CRM / Customer Platform seats and Sales Hub seats are separate ladders with different list prices; buying 'HubSpot' often means mixing Free CRM, Smart CRM seats, and hub seats.; Sales Hub Professional starts at $100/month per seat on the Product & Services Catalog and the Sales product page (re-checked 2026-08-18). HubSpot’s Sales pricing page also shows $90/mo/seat billed annually vs $100 monthly, plus required Professional onboarding ($1,500). Starter marketing prices show new-customer discounts (*).; Mailchimp: Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform; Paid pricing is contact-based and changes — verify live.

Poor-fit cases: HubSpot is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Smart CRM / Customer Platform seats and Sales Hub seats are separate ladders with different list prices; buying 'HubSpot' often means mixing Free CRM, Smart CRM seats, and hub seats. · Mailchimp is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Marketing-led CRM — not a full sales pipeline platform · Avoid HubSpot if you actually need Mailchimp's motion (Email marketing with CRM features; freemium entry (secondary category: marketing)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
